The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission has urged a High Court of the Federal Capital Territory to reject the bail application of a suspected fraudster, Adeniyi Adeyemi. The commission argued that his continued detention is necessary for his personal safety. The commission said some individuals who allegedly lost money to Adeyemi were searching for him and could physically harm him if released. Prosecution counsel, Sylvanus Tahir, SAN, made the submission on Wednesday while opposing the bail applications filed by Adeyemi and four civil servants charged alongside him over an alleged N27bn fraud involving a purported Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council. “My lord, there are many petitions against him, and the people who lodged those petitions are after him,” Tahir told the court. He cited the case of a petitioner from Ibadan who allegedly lost money to the defendant and had been searching for him. “We believe that it will be in his own best interest to remain in custody for safekeeping,” the prosecution counsel said. The ICPC also described Adeyemi as a flight risk, alleging that he had access to substantial funds and could interfere with some of the proposed witnesses. They have all been frozen. So he does not have the means to escape or to influence the witnesses,” Angulu said. Adeyemi and the four other defendants, Aminu Abdullahi, Ogaba Harry, Florence Omameh and Patricia Akhigbe, had pleaded not guilty to a 36-count amended charge bordering on obtaining money by false pretence, forgery and corruption. The defendants, through their respective lawyers, urged the court to admit them to bail, citing their constitutional rights to personal liberty and presumption of innocence, as well as provisions of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act. They also pleaded ill health and promised to attend subsequent proceedings. PHOTOS: Tinubu grants interview to American political strategist Diana London SERAP appeals N100m defamation award, awaits A’Court ruling NGE faults journalist’s remand, warns against press intimidation The prosecution, however, urged the court to reject the applications and order an accelerated hearing of the case. Justice Halilu Yusuf adjourned proceedings until November 30 for a ruling on the bail applications and commencement of trial. The judge ordered that the male defendants be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre, while the two female defendants were taken to the Suleja Correctional Centre. The ICPC had alleged that Adeyemi fraudulently presented himself as the Director-General of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council, which it described as a non-existent government agency, and obtained more than N27bn under the guise of establishing the organisation. He was also accused of obtaining another N3.8bn purportedly for the agency’s personnel costs. According to the commission, Adeyemi allegedly forged documents bearing the purported signature of the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, to portray himself as the agency’s director-general and secure government office facilities at the Federal Secretariat Complex, Phase III, Abuja. The four civil servants were allegedly involved in facilitating his activities. Abdullahi, an Assistant Chief Technical Officer in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, was accused of receiving N210,000 from Adeyemi to facilitate the allocation of office space. Harry, an official in the Office of the Chief Economic Adviser to the President, was also accused of receiving N300,000 to facilitate the release of two official vehicles — a Prado SUV and a Land Cruiser SUV — to the defendant. In another count, Adeyemi was accused of obtaining N20m on July 29, 2025, from Oyekunle Gbenga, Managing Director of Divine Dopacy Nigeria Limited, under the guise of a project facilitation loan for a purported N2.8bn contract awarded by the fictitious agency. The contract was allegedly for the procurement of furniture and renovation of the official residence of the agency’s purported director-general. The commission said the alleged offences were committed between 2024 and 2026. Adeyemi has been in detention since July 14 and was first arraigned on October 29. His re-arraignment on Wednesday followed an amendment of the charge to include the four civil servants.
